subject: CloudHarbor: sudden throughput collapse in eu-central — immediate steering request
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@cloudharbor.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: ops@cloudharbor.com
Date: 2026-04-18 03:45 UTC
Subject: Re: production errors and latency spike — CloudHarbor (eu-central)

Tessa —

We just hit a major regression in eu-central (eu-central-1) starting ~03:30 UTC. User-facing 5xx rate jumped to ~18% and p95 latency for text-generation climbed from ~210ms to ~950ms. Throughput dropped roughly 40% despite steady request volume — it looks like tail-latency + request queueing at the inference tier. Attached are a short sample of ingress headers and a rolling 30m CSV of request counts.

We have a scheduled traffic surge for a batch job but this is outside our expectations; it’s impacting our customers and our SLA. Can you run an immediate cross-region steer to eu-north or us-west while you investigate? We’re happy to accept any temporary model downgrade/quantized variant if it helps.

Attaching: cloudharbor_frontend_500s_20260418.log, traffic-report-20260418.csv, ops-screenshot-500s.png

Emma Li
SRE, CloudHarbor
emma@cloudharbor.com

Emma —

Thanks for the signal and the attachments. I’m escalating this to our on-call infra and reliability leads (below) and we’ll stand up a bridge now. Short plan we’ll execute immediately:

- Open incident bridge and correlate logs (INF-6743).
- Enable priority steer for CloudHarbor routing to route up to 35% of EU traffic to eu-north-1 while we validate.
- Temporarily allow cross-region fallback to us-west-2 if eu-north is capacity-constrained.
- Force-serve fallback model variant "redwood-small-quant" (lower memory) for CloudHarbor routes to reduce GPU pressure.
- Keep KV-prefix caching enabled; do NOT invalidate caches yet — that increases cold-starts.

Rishi / Hannah: please confirm if we can safely raise concurrency and enable quantized variant for their routes without violating other tenant SLAs. Marissa / Vivek: we’ll need a quick look at kernel saturation and whether a manual hardware drain/redispatch is required.

Sean — can you offer a short exec bridge to CloudHarbor leadership and note we’re prioritizing this?

I’ll keep everyone posted on the bridge and timeline.

Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-18 04:05 UTC
Subject: Re: production errors and latency spike — CloudHarbor (eu-central)

On it — preliminary telemetry:

- eu-central pod fleets show GPU kernel saturation on 2/3 hosting nodes for the model family used by CloudHarbor. Token processing stalls correlate with long KV cache lookup latencies.
- Request queue depth is increasing rather than being shed; our autoscaler did not trigger scale due to a mis-evaluated readiness probe (we have a follow-up).

Immediate actions I recommend (I can run these within 10m):
1) Bump concurrency per worker by +20% for CloudHarbor routes (short window) to allow in-flight completion while steer is activated.
2) Push model-> "redwood-small-quant" for their client key and lower token budget cap from 2048 -> 1024 for short term.
3) If kernel saturated persists, start manual instance replacement in eu-central-1a to relieve hot nodes — best-effort warm handoff.

Risk: concurrency bump + quantized model can increase latency variability for other tenants on same host; we’ll isolate by pinning CloudHarbor to dedicated pool if capacity allows. I’ll report back in 10m with a lift.

Rishi
Director, Runtime Ops

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-18 04:12 UTC
Subject: Re: production errors and latency spike — CloudHarbor (eu-central)

Agree with Rishi’s steps. Two operational notes:

- I need authorization to override the routing policy to allow immediate cross-region fallback for CloudHarbor routes (policy currently restricts to EU regions). This is a one-off exception for up to 6 hours. Approver: Tessa or Vivek.
- If we redirect >30% traffic, prefix caching effectiveness drops; recommend we warm caches in eu-north before ramping to 35%. I can spin up a warmup job to replay a small prompt set.

Marissa: can you validate that model-variant switch preserves the function/tool-calling behavior CloudHarbor uses? We should avoid changing any contract signatures.

Hannah
Sr. Reliability Engineer
